## What it is

- The **Stratocaster** is a solid-body electric guitar made by **Fender** (Wikipedia, "Fender Stratocaster").
- "Most Stratocasters have three single-coil pickups, a pickup selector switch, one volume control and two tone controls" (Wikipedia).
- Its selector was a 3-way switch at first; players found the in-between spots, and "Fender introduced a five-way selector in 1977" (Wikipedia).
- Its scale (string length from nut to bridge) is **25.5 inches** (648 mm) (Wikipedia).

## Its sound

- A pickup is a magnet with a coil of wire. The moving steel string changes the magnetic field and makes a small voltage in the coil.
- Where a pickup sits matters. A harmonic that has a still point (a *node*) over the pickup is not heard. So each place along the string hears a different set of harmonics: a *comb filter* (Tillman, 2002).
- The **neck** pickup is far from the bridge: it hears the low harmonics strongly, so it sounds round and warm. The **bridge** pickup is near the bridge: thinner and brighter.
- Positions **2** and **4** join two pickups. Their two combs add, and some harmonics cancel: the hollow "quack" (Wikipedia names position 2).
- Single coils pick up mains **hum**. On many Strats the middle pickup is wound the other way, so 2 and 4 cancel the hum (this page's model does that; unverified for any year).

## Guided tour

```{=html}
<div class="gt-step" data-guitar="strat" data-set="{&quot;sel&quot;:&quot;p5&quot;}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Position 5: neck.</b> Listen: round, warm, soft at the top.</p></div>
<div class="gt-step" data-guitar="strat" data-set="{&quot;sel&quot;:&quot;p3&quot;}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Position 3: middle.</b> A little brighter and thinner.</p></div>
<div class="gt-step" data-guitar="strat" data-set="{&quot;sel&quot;:&quot;p1&quot;}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Position 1: bridge.</b> Bright and thin, with bite.</p></div>
<div class="gt-step" data-guitar="strat" data-set="{&quot;sel&quot;:&quot;p2&quot;}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Position 2: bridge + middle.</b> Listen for the hollow "quack": some harmonics cancel.</p></div>
<div class="gt-step" data-guitar="strat" data-set="{&quot;sel&quot;:&quot;p4&quot;}" data-play="chord"><p><b>Position 4: middle + neck.</b> The quack again, warmer. Turn on <b>mains hum</b> above and compare 4 with 5: 4 is quiet.</p></div>
<div class="gt-step" data-guitar="strat" data-set="{&quot;sel&quot;:&quot;p5&quot;,&quot;tone1&quot;:0}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Neck, tone at 0.</b> The tone knob joins a capacitor to the signal. Listen: dark and woolly.</p></div>
<div class="gt-step" data-guitar="strat" data-set="{&quot;sel&quot;:&quot;p1&quot;,&quot;vol&quot;:6}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Bridge, volume at 6.</b> Quieter, and a little duller: the volume knob's resistance and the cable take treble away.</p></div>
```

## Works Cited

::: {.works-cited}
"Fender Stratocaster." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fender_Stratocaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fender_Stratocaster). Three single coils, one volume, two tones (neck; middle + bridge), five-way from 1977, position 2, 25.5 in, Clapton's Layla.

Lemme, Helmuth E. W. "The Secrets of Electric Guitar Pickups." [buildyourguitar.com/resources/lemme/](https://buildyourguitar.com/resources/lemme/). Resonance of most pickups with a normal cable 2,000-5,000 Hz; inductance 1-10 H (not read directly: certificate expired 2026-11-26; unverified).

"Pickup (music technology)." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pickup_(music_technology)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pickup_(music_technology)). Single coils pick up hum; humbucker coils cancel it; self-capacitance + cable resonate with the inductance; more turns, lower resonance.

Tillman, J. Donald. "Response Effects of Guitar Pickup Position and Width." 2000, updated 17 Oct. 2002. [www.till.com/articles/PickupResponse/index.html](https://www.till.com/articles/PickupResponse/index.html). Pickup point response sin(pi x F / (L F0)) = a comb filter; aperture term; Strat neck / middle / bridge 6.375 / 3.875 / 1.625 in, 1 in aperture; humbucker about 2.5 in; out-of-phase cancellation.
:::
